blocks.text: Setting up your Gmail environment on Mac

Most recruiters rely on Gmail for high-volume outreach. Because there is no native Gmail app for macOS, you must optimize your browser experience. Start by pinning Gmail to your Dock. In Safari, open Gmail, go to File > Add to Dock. This gives you a dedicated window. It prevents Gmail from getting lost among dozens of open browser tabs. If you use Chrome, go to the three-dot menu, select Save and Share > Install page as app. This creates a similar icon in your Applications folder.
Essential Gmail keyboard shortcuts for recruiters

Speed is vital when managing hundreds of candidate emails. First, enable shortcuts in Settings > General > Keyboard shortcuts. Once on, press ? to see the full list. As a recruiter, you should master a few core keys. Use c to compose a new message. Use e to archive an email you have processed. Use r to reply and a to reply all. Use j and k to move down and up through your inbox. These shortcuts save seconds on every interaction, adding up to hours over a week.

Organization prevents candidate drop-off. Create labels for each stage of your hiring process. Use labels like 01-Sourcing, 02-Screening, 03-Interview, and 04-Offer. You can color-code these labels to make your inbox visually clear. Right-click a label in the sidebar to choose a color. This helps you identify which candidates need urgent attention at a glance. If you are working with a team, consider using delegate access to allow assistants to help manage your inbox.

items: Do not exceed 500 recipients per day for personal accounts or 2,000 for Workspace accounts.
Avoid using third-party email clients that do not support OAuth, as they are less secure.
Check your connection if you see error 502, as this often indicates temporary service issues.
Use filters to automatically sort incoming resumes into specific folders based on keywords.

blocks.text: Lazur acts as your personal assistant while you are in Gmail. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about a candidate profile on your screen. Lazur can summarize text or help you draft a response. If you are stuck on a technical term in a resume, ask Lazur to explain it. You do not need to switch apps or open new tabs. This keeps your workflow focused on the candidate, not the software.

Scheduling consumes nearly half of a recruiter's day. Use tools like Calendly to automate this. Include your booking link in your Gmail signature. If you need to manually schedule, use the Gmail scheduling feature. Click the arrow next to the Send button and choose Schedule send. This ensures your emails land in the candidate's inbox at the right time. Being thoughtful about timing increases your response rate significantly.

When sending mass emails, always use BCC to protect candidate privacy. If you use CC, you expose every recipient's email address to the entire list. This is a major mistake that can damage your professional reputation. Use templates to speed up your outreach. Go to Settings > Advanced and enable Templates. This allows you to save frequently sent messages. You can then insert them into any new email with a few clicks.

Keep your notes in a separate app like Notion. When you receive an email with interview feedback, quickly copy it to your candidate's record. If you are overwhelmed, use the snooze feature. Click the clock icon to hide an email until a specific time. This clears your inbox of items you cannot address right now. It is a simple way to manage your mental load throughout the day.

faq.question: Is there a native Gmail app for Mac?
faq.answer: No, Google does not provide a native Gmail app for macOS. You should use a browser web app via Safari or Chrome for the best experience.

faq.question: How do I enable keyboard shortcuts in Gmail?
faq.answer: Go to Settings > General > Keyboard shortcuts and select the option to turn them on.

faq.question: What is the daily sending limit for Gmail?
faq.answer: Personal accounts can send to 500 recipients per day, while Workspace accounts can send to 2,000.

faq.question: How can Lazur help me with Gmail?
faq.answer: Lazur can help you draft emails, explain technical concepts found in resumes, and provide quick answers about your screen content without leaving Gmail.
